The PKGBUILD defines a standard VCS source using `git+https://github.com/kcat/openal-soft#tag=$pkgver`, which is a legitimate and expected method for fetching source code from a known upstream repository. The `b2sums` array contains a valid checksum for the commit/tag, but even if it were set to 'SKIP', that would not make this stage unsafe — missing or skipped checksums are not an execution risk during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, as they only affect verification, not execution.

The top-level scope of the PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments (e.g., `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`). There is no command substitution, no remote code execution, and no network activity triggered outside of the declared `source` array. The `pkgver()` function is not defined, so the static `pkgver=1.25.2` is used, posing no risk. No functions (`prepare`, `build`, `package_lib32-openal`) are executed due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags.

Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely fetch the source from the declared Git repository and parse the PKGBUILD without executing any potentially harmful code.
</details>
